apparatus.contract: ⛔ As throughout PG 88, every marker is printed in the LATIN column. No superscript appears anywhere in the Greek. The Greek chunks therefore carry NO [n:] markers — there is nothing in them to key one to. These notes attach to the ENGLISH at translation time.
apparatus.howToPlace: ⚑ THE NOTE'S OWN CITATION IS ITS LOCATOR. Migne prints the marker at the CLOSE OF THE SCRIPTURE QUOTATION the note names. Verified empirically 2026-08-07: of the eleven markers here, three survived the archive.org OCR of the Latin as `*`, and all three sit exactly at the end of the quotation they cite — `…sed ut convertatur et vivat *` (Ezech. xxxiii, 11), `…ad pœnitentiam *` (Matth. ix, 13), `…de crastino *` (Matth. vi, 34). So the translator places [n:] at the close of the quoted verse, using src/pg-latin/ to find where the quotation falls.
